sentences.text:
1) The present revision has been preferred challenging the order dated 27.01.2025 passed by the Court of Ms. Nidhi Bala, Ld. JMFC (Mahila Court), Shahdara, Karkardooma Court, Delhi in case FIR No.466/2014, under section 498A/406/354A/ 323/506/34 IPC & 4 DP Act vide which Ld.
JMFC had discharged accused Abdul Wahab in the above mentioned case.
2) The brief facts giving rise to the present revision are that Digitally signed by SUMEDH SUMEDH KUMAR SETHI KUMAR Date:
SETHI 2026.02.20 17:01:43 +0530 the complainant got married to the accused Abdul Wahab on 29.03.2008.

sentences.text:
The complainant got her FIR registered against her husband and other family members alleging cruelty for demand of dowry,
misappropriation of istreedhan of the complainant, and for hitting and misbehaving with the complainant.
It is averred in the petition that the charge sheet was filed against accused Abdul Wahab u/s 498A/406/354A/323/506/34 IPC and 4 DP Act.

It is further averred that the Ld. Court discharged the accused Abdul Wahab, from all State vs Abdul Wahab on 20 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107036511/
1 the offences vide order dated 27.01.2025.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the impugned order

,
petitioner/State has filed revision petition to challenge the said order.

3) The grounds for filing of the present revision are:
i.
That the impugned order is illegal and bad in eye of law and liable to be challenged because Ld. Trial court has committed illegality by discharging the accused Abdul Wahab, in the present case.

ii. That the Ld. JMFC failed to appreciate the well settled proposition that at the time of framing of charge it is only required to see whether a prima facie case is made out against the alleged accused on the basis of complaint and statement u/s 161 CrPC.
That court has failed to appreciate that at this stage meticulous evaluation of evidence is not required.

iii. That the Ld. JMFC failed to appreciate the well settled proposition of law that at the stage of framing charge it is not obligatory to consider in detail and to weigh in a sensitive balance whether the facts if proved, would be incompatible with the innocence of accused or not.
At that stage the court is not to SUMEDH KUMAR SETHI KUMAR

Date:
2026.02.20 SETHI 17:01:51 +0530 see whether there is sufficient ground for conviction.

Strong suspicion at the initial stage of framing of charge is sufficient to frame the charge and, in that event, it is not open to say that there is no sufficient ground for proceedings against the accused.

iv. The Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate the fact that the complainant had mentioned the specific allegation/ incident dated 01.07.2013 in her complaint in para no. 7 that is on 01.07.2013, the complainant was alone at her room, suddenly the dever of the complainant entered into her room and began to molest the complainant by touching her breast and hips.
The complainant raised alarm, then her husband came inside the room of the complainant and then accused Abdul Wahab and dever of the complainant gave beating to her mercilessly.
Then complainant came out of her room.
Then complainant's nand Rani and Mumtaji caught hold of the complainant from her hair and they also gave beatings to her by stick due to which she suffered severe injuries.
Mumu ajiz and Mamiya saas sehjadi of the accused abdul wahab were also there and they were instigating by saying "isko to aj maar dalo baki hum dekh lenge".

Then the complainant made the call on 100 no.; in between the accused Abdul Wahab snatched the mobile phone of the complainant from her hands and ran away from the spot while threatening her by saying that "tujhe to main jann se maar doonga".
Devar of the complainant also threatened the complainant by saying "aj to maine tujhe chore diya parantu aager tera haal isse bhi bura hoga".

2 v. The Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate the fact that the contents of the FIR and her other statements are disclosing SUMEDH by SUMEDH KUMAR SETHI KUMAR Date:
SETHI 2026.02.20 17:01:57 +0530 the allegations against the Abdul Wahab and are enough to frame charges against the accused.
4) Notice of the revision was given to the respondent Abdul Wahab.
Trial court record was requisitioned.
Arguments heard.
Material on record perused.
Submissions considered.
5) No reply to the present revision was filed on behalf of respondent.

6) Ld. Addl. PP for the State/revisionist has relied upon the case of State of Rajasthan vs. Ashok Kumar Kashyap (Cr. Appeal No.407 of 2021) decided by Hon'ble Supreme Court to contend that at the stage of framing of charge and/or considering the discharge application, mini trial is not permissible.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan vs. Ashok Kumar Kashyap (Cr. Appeal No.407 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Only the court has to see whether or not a prima facie case is made out.

It is also argued that in her complaint dated 01.07.2013, the complainant had leveled specific allegations against the brother of the respondent regarding outraging her modesty and against other accused regarding their instigation to kill the complainant.
It is argued that these specific averments could not be ignored at this stage and their truth or falsity has to be decided during trial.

7) Ld. Counsel for the respondent submits that the Ld. Trial Court has rightly discharged the accused Abdul Wahab, as the complainant leveled specific allegations against the father of the respondent in the year 2013 whereas the said person had expired in 2004.

Further, reference has been made by the Ld. Trial Court to the supplementary charge-sheet which contains the first version of events pertaining to 01.07.2013 which are totally SUMEDH by SUMEDH KUMAR Date:
2026.02.20 SETHI 17:02:04 +0530 different from the complaint dated 01.07.2013 which has been made the basis of the present revision petition.

It is argued that in the first version of events pertaining to the date 01.07.2013, the complainant has not made any allegations which are seen in the complaint on the basis of which the orders u/s 156 Cr. P. C. were passed by the Magistrate concerned for registration of FIR.
It is argued that the material contradictions and improvements caste a shadow of doubt on the veracity of the complaint as a whole.
8) This court finds that the complaint dated 01.07.2013 which forms the basis of the present FIR contains allegations against the respondent and his various relatives.

In the revision petition, it has been prayed that the order dated 27.01.2025 passed by the Ld. JMFC discharging the respondent should be set aside and charges should be framed against the respondent for the offences for which he has been charge-sheeted.

However, perusal of record shows that on the basis of this very complaint and the allegations leveled therein, all the relatives of the respondent mentioned in the memo of parties in the said complaint except for the respondent himself were kept in State vs Abdul Wahab on 20 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107036511/
3 column no.12 of the charge-sheet and only the respondent was kept in column no.11.
Vide order dated 21.09.2017, even the ld. JMFC concerned chose to summon only the respondent who was kept in column no.11 of the charge-sheet and not those who were kept in column no.12.
This order has not been challenged by the prosecution.

This court is of the opinion that if the allegations leveled in the complaint dated 01.07.2013 were the only consideration to be blindly followed for the purpose of proceeding against those against whom allegations have been made then, there is no discernible differentia between the respondent and the other relatives that the SUMEDH by SUMEDH KUMAR Date:
2026.02.20 SETHI 17:02:09 +0530 State would choose to pursue the case before the Magistrate and before this court only against the present respondent and not against his other relatives.
9)

Further, the court is also of the opinion that if mere allegations were to form the basis of framing of charge then no matter how absurd the allegations, charge would have to be framed without fail in all cases and the provisions for discharge would be rendered redundant.
For instance, if one was to allege something as absurd as stealing the moon then it would be equally absurd to frame charges of theft merely on the basis of such allegations.

10) Thus, there has to be at least a prima facie scrutiny of the allegations leveled in the complaint and for this purpose, it is not as if one line or the other of the complaint have to be dissected and seen in a piece-meal fashion or in isolation but the complaint has to be seen as an organic document as a whole.

11) The Ld. Trial court has rightly analyzed the complaint and has rightly opined that the complaint contains allegations against the father of the respondent who died about ten years prior to the allegations being leveled.
This fact has not been disputed.

Further, in the supplementary charge-sheet filed by the IO, the first version of the events pertaining to 01.07.2013 has been mentioned which is completely different from the complaint dated 01.07.2013 which forms the basis of the FIR and the charge-sheet.

Trial court has rightly considered these contradictions and improvements as from the perusal of record it is apparent Digitally signed by SUMEDH SUMEDH KUMAR SETHI KUMAR Date:
SETHI 2026.02.20 17:02:15 +0530 that almost all of the allegations leveled in the complaint dated 01.07.2013 are an afterthought and the incident has been spruced up to sensationalize the case and make it appear more serious.

The complaint dated 01.07.2013 is not a mere explanation or enhancement of the original allegations mentioned in the supplementary charge-sheet but a complete re-imagination of the State vs Abdul Wahab on 20 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107036511/
4 entire incident.

It is noteworthy that the version mentioned in the supplementary charge-sheet is a reproduction of a kalandra prepared pursuant to the PCR call, as has been mentioned by the Ld.
Trial court.
This fact has not been disputed.

It is not as if the complainant has sought further investigation or filed protest petition against the supplementary charge-sheet despite the complainant being present regularly before the Trial court with her counsel and the FIR being registered on the basis of her application under section 156 (3) CrPC.
13)
It is settled law that where there are no chances of conviction despite the material on record being taken as it is then the accused ought to be discharged.
No useful purpose will be served by multiplying authorities on this point.

This court is of the opinion that in view of the glaring material contradictions and improvements in the complaint as a whole, it would be difficult to base conviction on the basis of bald allegations leveled therein especially when it has come on record that the complainant did not even co-operate with the investigation in supplying documents such as bills etc. in support of her complaint.
14) Therefore, this court does not find any ground to interfere with the order of Ld. Trial Court passed on 27.01.2025 whereby the respondent was discharged.

Consequently, the revision Digitally signed by SUMEDH SUMEDH KUMAR SETHI KUMAR Date:
SETHI 2026.02.20 17:02:34 +0530 petition is dismissed.
15) Copy of this order alongwith Trial Court Record be sent to Ld. Trial Court for information.
Revision stands disposed of.
16) Revision file be consigned to Record Room.
